messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: elevated tail latency and regional rising error rate for us-east-1 -> backend timeouts 504s. p99 > 1.1s for last 10m. Paging @anya_oncall and SRE rotation.
anya_oncall: I'm awake. Looking at region heatmaps and routing decisions. Lucy, can you pull request attribution by region+tier?
lucy_prod: grabbing. Quick summary: sudden spike in us-east long context requests from standard tier. Also seeing bursty cross-region egress to eu-west caused by geo-fallbacks.
diego_sre: KV cache thrash metrics spiking in us-east nodes; some hosts hit kernel fallback to slow int8 path. Suspect large-seq churn + cache eviction.
ellie_support: Multiple customers flagged slow responses; one enterprise (MediStream) saw increased errors. They're in US and are marked premium.
anya_oncall: MediStream should be routed to dedicated-us-east; logs show their tokens are flapping between dataplane clusters because of ephemeral IPs. Routing policy seems to be evaluating location by client IP first then token mapping. That sequence may misclassify when proxying occurs.
anya_oncall: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) Pin premium tokens to dedicated-us-east via emergency override 2) Temporarily throttle standard/free long-seq requests (seq>1024) 3) Enable regional capacity burst for us-east (borrow from dedicated pool) 4) Notify CSMs. Thoughts?
lucy_prod: +1. Recommend canary the token pin to 2% first, verify no route flapping.
diego_sre: For throttle rule, let's do token-tier + seq-length based shaping. Rule: if token_tier in [standard, free] AND seq_len>1024 => rps_per_token 5 and reject-after-queue 50ms.
ops-bot: Suggested CLI snippet: ```redctl route apply --policy emergency-pin-us-east.json --canary 2% --note "pin premium tokens to us-east; seq throttle"```
deploy-bot: policy apply initiated (ch: ch_pin_177351). Canary 2% rolling.
anya_oncall: Canary results: pin slice p99 -> 220ms, error rate stable. But watch for cross-region cost spike; routing to dedicated increases cost.
ellie_support: MediStream reports partial improvement on canary slice. They're asking for a timeline.
anya_oncall: We'll expand to 25% now to catch more premium traffic. If all good, move to 100% in 10m.
deploy-bot: rollout 25% (ch: ch_pin_177351). Monitoring: overall us-east p95 improved, cross-region egress up 18%.
lucy_prod: Noting cost vs latency tradeoff. We should also tune fallback order: prefer token-mapping over geo by default for enterprise tier. Add to post-incident actions.
diego_sre: throttle rule in effect for seq>1024 on standard/free. Queue depth decreased and KV miss rate fell 30% on slices.
anya_oncall: Increasing to 100% now.
deploy-bot: rollout 100% complete (ch: ch_pin_177351). Status: success.
incident-bot: Mitigation applied: premium pin to dedicated-us-east, seq-length throttles for non-premium, temporary capacity borrow. Customer impact reduced from ~21% affected -> ~4%. p99 us-east at ~340ms.
ellie_support: MediStream confirmed improvement; CSM updating them. No other enterprise escalations open.
anya_oncall: Handoff plan: I'll monitor for 45m then hand to @diego_sre for overnight watch. Handoff notes: change-id ch_pin_177351; revert command: ```redctl route revert ch_pin_177351```. Reversion threshold: if error rate goes above baseline +0.5% or p99 worsens by 200ms.
lucy_prod: Post-incident items: - audit token->cluster mapping logic - make pinning a first-class action in runbooks - add synthetic sim for proxy+ip-flapping scenario - cost-analysis for borrow flow.\diego_sre: I will follow up with kernel team about fallback heuristics under KV pressure.
anya_oncall: Also toggled a temporary feature-flag to disable large-seq auto-extend for standard/free: ```features.large_seq_auto_extend = off for tiers standard,free```. Logged in timeline.
incident-bot: Incident record created (inc_id: inc_177351). Update posted to ops-log.
anya_oncall: Thanks all. Diego taking the pager at T+45. Leaving link to timeline and metrics snapshot in #incidents-docs. 
anya_oncall: Marking this as mitigation-success for now. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem. :white_check_mark:
